% Written by `lab paper puzzle-difficulty`; do not edit by hand.
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{lL}
\toprule
Feature & Description \\
\midrule
\texttt{material\_count} & The total material of both sides, counting a pawn as 1, a knight as 3, a bishop as 3.25, a rook as 5 and a queen as 9. \\
\texttt{material\_imbalance} & The mover's material minus the opponent's, on the same scale. \\
\texttt{phase\_piece\_count} & The number of knights, bishops, rooks and queens on the board, both sides together. \\
\texttt{in\_check} & Whether the mover is in check. \\
\texttt{legal\_moves} & The number of legal moves the mover has. \\
\texttt{legal\_captures} & The number of the mover's legal moves that are captures. \\
\texttt{legal\_checks} & The number of the mover's legal moves that give check. \\
\texttt{hanging\_own} & The number of the mover's pieces that are attacked by a less valuable piece, or attacked and not defended. \\
\texttt{hanging\_opponent} & The number of the opponent's pieces that are attacked by a less valuable piece, or attacked and not defended. \\
\texttt{passed\_pawns\_own} & The number of the mover's pawns with no enemy pawn ahead of them on their own or an adjacent file. \\
\texttt{passed\_pawns\_opponent} & The number of the opponent's pawns with no enemy pawn ahead of them on their own or an adjacent file. \\
\texttt{attackers\_near\_own\_king} & The number of attacks by the opponent on the squares adjacent to the mover's king. \\
\texttt{attackers\_near\_opponent\_king} & The number of attacks by the mover on the squares adjacent to the opponent's king. \\
\texttt{first\_piece} & The piece that makes the first move of the line, from pawn (1) to king (6). \\
\texttt{first\_capture} & Whether the first move of the line is a capture. \\
\texttt{first\_captured\_value} & The value of the piece captured by the first move of the line. \\
\texttt{first\_check} & Whether the first move of the line gives check. \\
\texttt{first\_promotion} & Whether the first move of the line promotes a pawn. \\
\texttt{first\_distance} & The distance covered by the first move, in king moves (Chebyshev distance). \\
\texttt{first\_backward} & Whether the first move goes backward, towards the mover's own side of the board. \\
\texttt{first\_to\_attacked} & Whether the destination square of the first move is attacked by the opponent. \\
\texttt{first\_sacrifice} & Whether the piece moved first can be captured on its destination square, by a less valuable piece or while undefended, having captured less than its own value. \\
\texttt{line\_checks} & The number of the solver's moves that give check. \\
\texttt{line\_captures} & The number of the solver's moves that are captures. \\
\texttt{line\_quiet} & The number of the solver's moves that are neither captures nor checks. \\
\texttt{line\_promotions} & The number of the solver's moves that promote a pawn. \\
\texttt{line\_pieces\_moved} & The number of different pieces the solver moves. \\
\texttt{line\_sacrifices} & The number of the solver's moves that sacrifice material. \\
\texttt{line\_max\_distance} & The largest distance covered by one of the solver's moves. \\
\texttt{ends\_in\_mate} & Whether the line ends in checkmate. \\
\texttt{reply\_captures} & The number of the opponent's replies in the line that are captures. \\
\texttt{setup\_capture} & Whether the opponent's move that leads to the position was a capture. \\
\texttt{final\_material\_gain} & The material balance after the line minus the balance before it. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
